content.theory:
`String` is an object, so it has built-in **methods** — actions you call on it with `.method()`:

```java
String text = "Hello, World";

System.out.println(text.length());         // 12
System.out.println(text.toUpperCase());    // HELLO, WORLD
System.out.println(text.toLowerCase());    // hello, world
System.out.println(text.trim());           // removes surrounding spaces
System.out.println(text.charAt(0));        // H
System.out.println(text.substring(0, 5));  // Hello
System.out.println(text.indexOf("World")); // 7
```

**Important gotcha:** strings are immutable — methods like `toUpperCase()` return a *new* string rather than changing the original:

```java
String name = "sam";
name.toUpperCase();        // does nothing useful — result discarded
String fixed = name.toUpperCase();  // correct: store the result
```

Compare strings with `.equals()` — never `==` (that compares references, not content):

```java
if (password.equals("secret")) { ... }
```

**Escape sequences**: `\n` (newline), `\t` (tab), `\"` (quote).
